title: Hybrid commit credit slice playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick running notes for a hybrid commit model that slices reserved capacity into small, time-boxed credit bundles. Target audience: internal PM + finance to prototype offers for early enterprise customers who want predictable throughput but still want pay-as-you-go flexibility.

High-level idea:
- Sell small monthly commitments ("slices") that purchase guaranteed throughput/credits. Customers can stitch slices together or supplement with PAYG tokens for bursts. Each slice is priced to reflect reserved GPU amortization + ops premium + SLA uplift.
- Slices expire at period end (30d) but can roll into a short buffer (72 hours) to smooth burst usage.
- Incentivize multi-slice purchases with volume discounts and an SLA credit (refund) for missed latency/availability targets.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Avg production model: 8k context, 10 requests/sec sustained per large customer during peak hour; mean tokens per request: 1.2k (input+output).
- Serving efficiency: 80 tokens/sec/GPU (conservative for quantized Llama-like on A100-equivalent).
- Billable tokens per second per GPU: 80 tps -> 80 * 3600 * 24 = 6,912,000 tokens/day ~ 200M tokens/month (30d).
- Infra cost: $6.00/GPU-hour (inclusive of infra amortization), ops+overhead add 30% -> $7.80/GPU-hour total.
- Effective GPU-hours covered by 1 slice: decide target coverage = 10 GPU-hours/day for a month -> 300 GPU-hours -> cost = 300 * 7.8 = $2,340 cost per slice.

Translate to token coverage: 1 slice token-capacity ~ 300 hrs * 3600 s/hr * 80 tps = 86,400,000 tokens/month.
So cost per token (CPT) = $2,340 / 86.4M = $0.0000271 per token (~0.0271 mills).

Pricing knobs to play with:
- Anchored retail: 3x CPT -> $0.000081/token retail (rounded to $0.00008).
- Volume discounts: 10 slices -> 20% off baseline -> $0.000064/token.
- SLA uplift: +10% price for 99.9% latency SLO vs best-effort.
- Burn friction: expired-slice rollover of 72h allowed, beyond that tokens converted to discounted PAYG credit at 25% of retail to avoid wasted revenue.

Example customer scenarios:
1) Small team (1 slice): pays $2,340 -> provides ~86M tokens/month. If they use only 50% (43M), effective CPT doubles due to unused capacity but perceived value is guaranteed latency and burst coverage.
2) Mid: 4 slices w/ 5% discount -> effective price = 2,340 * 0.95 * 4 = $8,892 for 345M tokens -> retail CPT ~ $0.0000257/token (after discount).
3) Enterprise: 20 slices + SLA -> 20 * 2,340 * 0.8 (vol disc) * 1.1 (sla uplift) = ~$41k/month -> token capacity 1.728B -> CPT ~ $0.0000238/token.

Hybrid PAYG top-up logic:
- PAYG priced at retail CPT (3x baseline) so slices remain attractive for committed predictable workloads.
- If slice fully exhausted, routing rules: (1) short-burst allowance (throttle) up to 5 minutes at PAYG; (2) automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized model variant at same latency tier (if quality acceptable); (3) optional overage charge if customer opts-in (flat per-token surcharge).

Experiment matrix (A/B):
- Axis A: Slice size (1, 5, 10 GPU-hours/day equivalents).
- Axis B: Rollover policy (no-roll, 72h buffer, 30% rollover).
- Axis C: Price multiple (2.5x, 3x, 4x CPT).
Metrics to track:
- Activation conversion (trial -> first slice purchase).
- Burn rate: fraction of slice tokens used within period. Target >60% for sustainable economics.
- Churn correlated with underutilization and SLA breaches.
- Upsell: customers adding slices vs buying PAYG.

Risks / open questions:
- Model-level variability: our 80 tps assumption can be wrong by ±30% across families. Need per-model conversion factors baked into slice definitions.
- Sales complexity: many small slices might create overhead for billing and enable arbitrage across regions. Consider minimum slice unit to reduce complexity.
- Accounting: revenue recognition for committed slices may require deferral handling. Check finance.

Next steps (short):
- Build simple spreadsheet that parameterizes slices by GPU-hours/day, price multiplier, discount tiers; allow sensitivity to tps and gpu cost.
- Simulate 3 customer archetypes across 6 months to estimate churn and ARPU uplift.
- Draft a 1-pager for Sales with simple selling points: predictable unit price, burst protection, SLA option, simple add-on top-up.

Notes to self:
- Cross-check our GPU-hour cost with infra team (Ravi).
- Add model family multipliers (m1 small, m2 large) to the spreadsheet.
- Link to confluence draft: confluence:PRICING/hybrid-slices (placeholder)

Rough spreadsheet columns to implement now:
- slice_id, gpu_hours_per_day, monthly_gpu_hours, token_capacity_month, base_cost_slice, retail_multiplier, retail_price_slice, discount_band, net_price, expected_utilization_pct, effective_cpt, notes

End of playbook scratchpad.
